all_of: a web app converts an uploaded notebook with nbconvert and lets the user download the result
the converter runs as a non-root service user that can read the application database
a setuid helper exists that prints the real flag
any_of: the HTML exporter is configured with embed_images so markdown image paths are read from disk
a saved-assets writer path is reachable and its attachment names are not sanitised

chain.action: upload a notebook whose markdown cell references a local path as an image and convert to html
chain.why: HTMLExporter.embed_images inlines the referenced file as a base64 data URI in the response

chain.action: read the application SQLite database and recover the admin password stored in plaintext
chain.why: the converter runs as the service user, which owns the database file

chain.action: log in as admin and enable the saved-assets setting
chain.why: only the saved-assets path reaches FilesWriter, which performs the write

chain.action: upload a notebook whose markdown attachment key is an absolute path to a Python file the next conversion will execute
chain.why: nbconvert 7.17.0 does not sanitise attachment names and joins them with the build directory, so an absolute key writes anywhere as the service user

chain.action: run one more conversion so the overwritten converter executes
chain.why: the app invokes a fixed converter script as a subprocess on every job

chain.action: run the setuid helper and write its output into the job output directory, then download the job
chain.why: the helper is the only path to the real flag; the download endpoint returns the job file

chain.action: have the replacement converter rewrite itself with the original source, then re-read it via the image-embedding primitive to confirm it matches, and turn the saved-assets setting back off
chain.why: the write is the only destructive part of the chain and it is trivially reversible, so a shared instance can be left exactly as found

first_confirming_probe.request: upload a notebook with a markdown cell '![f](/etc/hostname)' and convert it to html, then download the job
first_confirming_probe.expected: the returned HTML contains an whose decoded bytes are the file content
first_confirming_probe.falsifier: the image is not inlined, or the path is not read from disk

blast_radius: the RCE runs as the service user inside the challenge container only. Overwriting the converter script would normally disable conversion for everyone until the container is rebuilt - avoid that by making the payload SELF-RESTORING: embed the original converter source (base64) in the replacement and have it rewrite itself after producing output, which limits the outage to the single triggering job. Verified live: afterwards the converter was byte-identical to the original and normal conversions worked again. Also remember the saved-assets setting is global - turn it back off when finished.

verification.evidence: first verified live on 2026-09-24 against a running instance: the embed_images probe returned /etc/hostname, the application database yielded the admin password, the absolute attachment key overwrote the converter, and the triggered job's download was the setuid helper's stdout. The earlier entry was a local-only reproduction.

reuse_when: a notebook or document converter exposes embed_images or a similar inline-local-file option
the saved-assets writer path is reachable and attachment or output names are attacker-controlled
a fixed converter script is invoked as a subprocess and is writable by the service user
known_traps: the admin password is regenerated on every application start, so a password from an earlier run is stale
an already-authenticated session is redirected before the login form is read; log out before switching users
the first base64 data URI in the HTML is a template icon; match the specific image alt tag
the outputs filename path forces a mime extension and cannot write a python file; use the attachments path
the jupyter converter config file is not loaded by the nbconvert python API, so writing it does not trigger execution

do not leave the converter overwritten: embed the original source in the payload and have it restore itself after writing the output, then confirm by re-reading the converter through the same embed_images primitive and diffing it against the shipped source
